title: Adic quotients of a finite-type localization are unchanged after completing the local base
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring (local means having the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\widehat R=\varprojlim_n R/\mathfrak m^n$ be its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion with canonical map $\iota:R\to\widehat R$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $C$ be a finite-type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime ideal of $C$ containing $\mathfrak mC$. Put $D=C\otimes_R\widehat R$ [def-weil-module-base-change, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(c\otimes a)(c'\otimes a')=cc'\otimes aa'$ and unit $1\otimes1$, and structural maps $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. If $Q$ is a prime ideal of $D$ whose contraction to $C$ is $\mathfrak q$ and whose contraction to $\widehat R$ is its maximal ideal, then for every $n\geq1$ the canonical local map $C_{\mathfrak q}\to D_Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] induces an isomorphism
$$C_{\mathfrak q}/(\mathfrak qC_{\mathfrak q})^n\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Q/(QD_Q)^n.$$
These isomorphisms commute with the quotient transition maps for all $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 00MA(3), together with the finite-type affine localization and quotient calculation written in the proof of this node

proof.text: Write $f:C\to D$, $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. Since $R$ is Noetherian, its ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated. For each $n\geq1$, apply the completion-mod-power statement to $(R,\mathfrak m)$: the projection $\pi_n:\widehat R\to R/\mathfrak m^n$ is a surjective $R$-algebra map, $\pi_n\iota$ is reduction, and $\ker\pi_n=\mathfrak m^n\widehat R$. Also $\widehat R$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat R$ by the local-completion statement. Thus all these assertions apply to the particular completion in the hypotheses.

Fix $n\geq1$ and put $E_n=C/\mathfrak q^n$. Because $\mathfrak mC\subseteq\mathfrak q$, products of $n$ elements of $\mathfrak m$ act as zero on $E_n$; hence the structural map $R\to E_n$ factors through $R/\mathfrak m^n$. Compose this factor with $\pi_n$ to obtain $\theta_n:\widehat R\to E_n$. The $R$-balanced bilinear map $(c,a)\mapsto\bar c\theta_n(a)$ defines an $R$-linear map $b_n:D\to E_n$ by the tensor-product universal property. It is a ring map: on pure tensors multiplicativity is $\overline{cc'}\theta_n(aa')=(\bar c\theta_n(a))(\bar c'\theta_n(a'))$, and distributivity gives the assertion for finite sums; it preserves the unit as well. Since $b_n(f(c))=\bar c$, it kills $\mathfrak q^nD$ and induces $\beta_n:D/\mathfrak q^nD\to E_n$. Conversely $f$ induces $\alpha_n:E_n\to D/\mathfrak q^nD$, and $\beta_n\alpha_n=1$.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), quotient calculation using the tensor universal property in Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: For $a\in\widehat R$, choose $r\in R$ representing $\pi_n(a)$. Step 1 gives $a-\iota(r)\in\mathfrak m^n\widehat R$. Write this difference as a finite sum $\sum_j\iota(t_j)a_j$ with $t_j\in\mathfrak m^n$ and $a_j\in\widehat R$. For every $c\in C$, balancing gives $c\otimes(a-\iota(r))=\sum_j ct_j\otimes a_j\in\mathfrak q^nD$, since $t_jC\subseteq\mathfrak q^n$. Therefore in $D/\mathfrak q^nD$ the class of $c\otimes a$ equals that of $cr\otimes1$, which is $\alpha_n\beta_n$ of the former class. Pure tensors generate $D$ additively, so $\alpha_n\beta_n=1$. Thus $\alpha_n$ is a ring isomorphism for every $n$, induced by $f$.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), kernel formula and explicit inverse calculation

proof.text: At $n=1$ we have $D/\mathfrak qD\cong C/\mathfrak q$ with the map from $C$ equal to reduction. Since $f^{-1}(Q)=\mathfrak q$, the ideal $Q$ contains $\mathfrak qD$. If $d\in Q$, surjectivity of $\alpha_1$ gives $c\in C$ with $d-f(c)\in\mathfrak qD$. Then $f(c)\in Q$, so $c\in\mathfrak q$ and $d\in\mathfrak qD$. Consequently $Q=\mathfrak qD$. Extension of ideals commutes with taking powers: both $(\mathfrak qD)^n$ and $\mathfrak q^nD$ are generated by the images of products of $n$ elements of $\mathfrak q$. In particular $Q^n=\mathfrak q^nD$, and $\alpha_n$ identifies the prime $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q^n$ of $E_n$ with $Q/Q^n$ of $D/Q^n$.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), elementary ideal calculation after the n=1 quotient comparison

proof.text: Since $f^{-1}(Q)=\mathfrak q$, the map $f$ induces $f_{\mathrm{loc}}:C_{\mathfrak q}\to D_Q$, $c/s\mapsto f(c)/f(s)$. The inverse image of $QD_Q$ is $\mathfrak qC_{\mathfrak q}$: a fraction is in the maximal ideal exactly when its numerator is in the prime, by the localization-at-prime description. Apply the localization-of-a-quotient statement to $(C,\mathfrak q^n,\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q^n)$ and $(D,Q^n,Q/Q^n)$. It identifies the desired source and target with $(C/\mathfrak q^n)_{\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q^n}$ and $(D/Q^n)_{Q/Q^n}$, respectively. Here $\mathfrak q^nC_{\mathfrak q}=(\mathfrak qC_{\mathfrak q})^n$ and $Q^nD_Q=(QD_Q)^n$ by the same product-of-generators calculation as in Step 4. The isomorphism $\alpha_n$ and its inverse carry the complements of these primes to each other. On fractions they induce inverse maps $\bar c/\bar s\mapsto\overline{f(c)}/\overline{f(s)}$ and its inverse. Under the quoted identifications this is exactly the map induced by $f_{\mathrm{loc}}$, so that map on quotients is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), applied at the two primes; Tag 00CO (definition-localization)

proof.text: For $k\geq n\geq1$, both composites from $C_{\mathfrak q}/(\mathfrak qC_{\mathfrak q})^k$ to $D_Q/(QD_Q)^n$ send the class of every fraction $c/s$ to the class of $f(c)/f(s)$. Such classes exhaust the source. Thus the square of quotient transition maps commutes. In particular all the isomorphisms are induced by the one canonical local map, as asserted.
